summary: The existing primitives support phases 1–2, but only if experts remain inert bundles and the resolver is an adapter over current prompt, retrieval, policy, and decision planes. The main risks are shared PromptBuilder mutation, authored-text substitution, treating prompt rules as enforcement, and importing dev-loop-specific gate types into a general runtime.

suggestions.title: Implement a sibling ExpertDirectoryLoader and ExpertRegistry
suggestions.rationale: AgentRegistry owns executable BotMetadata, factories, singleton instances, tooling, and lenient duplicate handling. Reusing it would make an inert manifest executable and inherit unsuitable lifecycle semantics. Follow the deterministic directory-loading pattern of SkillsDirectoryLoader, but use a strict ExpertManifest and an explicit duplicate/shadowing report.

suggestions.title: Make expert activation an ephemeral prompt projection
suggestions.rationale: PromptBuilder is a name-keyed map with one replaceable identity slot, and configure() permanently resolves its layers. Activation should clone a pristine builder and return a per-request projection; it must not mutate a shared bot. Phase 1 should either allow only one inline expert or define namespaced expert layers before claiming multi-expert composition.

suggestions.title: Force all bundle-authored text through literal prompt layers
suggestions.rationale: PromptLayer performs string.Template substitution by default, while load_identity() defaults to unescaped file content. A persona or rule containing $name, $role, or malicious placeholder syntax can therefore be rewritten during configure(). Expert persona, knowledge, and governance content should be emitted with literal=True, with a regression test proving authored dollar expressions remain unchanged.

suggestions.title: Add KnowledgeResolver beside the existing KB path before replacing it
suggestions.rationale: AbstractBot currently combines PageIndex, vector, and KB material into knowledge_content, while KBSelector performs optional LLM-based activation. Replacing this path in the first resolver release would couple a new manifest feature to a large request lifecycle with dormant coverage. Introduce a resolver that returns a KnowledgeContext and adapt its rendered output into the existing knowledge layer; preserve register_kb and KBSelector until equivalent behavior is proven.

suggestions.title: Make KnowledgeContext structured, attributable, and budget-aware
suggestions.rationale: GraphIndex retrieval already exposes typed ContextBundle evidence and digests; DecisionService bounds output with budget_tokens; LLMWikiToolkit applies its own fixed packing budget. A resolver that concatenates source strings would lose provenance and make trimmed reporting unverifiable. Require per-source entries, deterministic ordering, token counts, source fingerprints, and an explicit trimmed flag before rendering the final prompt layer.

suggestions.title: Use explicit namespace and link mappings for v1 knowledge scope
suggestions.rationale: LLMWikiToolkit.query accepts wiki_name but no tag filter, DecisionRecord has status and links but no tags, and BookCard.topics is the only tag-like catalog field. A generic scope.tags contract would be unimplementable consistently. Define v1 scope as an exact wiki namespace plus accepted-ADR filtering by links and bookstore topic matching; keep write/review capabilities outside the resolver.

suggestions.title: Enforce non-delegation in tool authorization and nesting state
suggestions.rationale: The actual delegation tool is spawn_sub_agent, whose restriction is an allowlist; no deny-list or nesting guard exists. Prompt rules cannot enforce the invariant. Compile the expert tool allowlist without spawn_sub_agent, add a ToolManager/PBAC denial for defense in depth, and bind a task-local nesting/owner guard so a direct or nested attempt returns forbidden even if the model requests it.

suggestions.title: Defer stage binding and preserve existing crew/flow contracts
suggestions.rationale: CrewDefinition is extra-forbid and has no lead/support vocabulary; FlowDefinition currently contains generic NodeDefinition(id,type) plus edges. Adding stage fields or dispatch modes without a compiler would either fail validation or leak orchestration semantics into crews. Keep phase 1–2 independent of stages and specify a later ExpertStageNode compiler rather than extending AgentDefinition opportunistically.

suggestions.title: Adapt ApprovalGate instead of creating a third gate stack
suggestions.rationale: ApprovalGate carries the needed TTL, fail-open/fail-closed, payload_ref, and audit semantics, but its GateKind and NodeId are closed to dev-loop values. The human package is a separate channel-facing interaction model. If a generic gate is needed later, extract a protocol with string identifiers and provide a compatibility adapter for persisted ApprovalGate envelopes; do not import dev-loop literals into expert runtime or duplicate HITL behavior.

suggestions.title: Make negative isolation and concurrency tests release gates
suggestions.rationale: The critical contracts are failure behaviors: malformed manifests do not activate, duplicate IDs are deterministic, workspace precedence is stable, $placeholders remain literal, missing wiki scope is distinguished from empty retrieval, budgets report trimming, two concurrent activations cannot cross-contaminate builders, and spawn_sub_agent is forbidden. These tests should exercise the existing loader, prompt, retrieval, manager, and ContextVar seams rather than only snapshotting final prompts.
